seo.title: TablePro vs DbGate: editions and supported platforms
seo.description: DbGate is an open-source client for Windows, macOS, Linux and the web, with paid Premium editions. TablePro is open source and native on Mac and iPhone.

header.title: TablePro vs DbGate
header.lead: DbGate offers desktop and web clients, built on {technology}. Compare its Community and Premium editions with TablePro’s native client.

tablepro: Free AI chat with your choice of provider.
AWS IAM and Microsoft Entra ID sign-in without a paid tier.
Free backups through supported engines’ dump tools.
competitor: A client for Windows, Linux or a web server.
Firebird, Azure Cosmos DB or Firestore connections.
A visual query designer in {cells.queryDesigner.edition}, or DbGate Cloud sync.

glance.intro: DbGate has a free Community edition and Premium and Team Premium editions billed per user, so several rows say which edition a feature needs.

diagram.label: ER diagram
diagram.tablepro: A read-only ER diagram, exported as PNG or SQL, free

modelCompare.label: Compare database models
modelCompare.tablepro: Compare & Sync compares the structure or the data of two databases and writes the sync script. Part of Starter

backup.label: Backup and restore
backup.tablepro: Free in the Mac app: Backup Dump and Restore Dump through the engine’s own dump tool, where it has one

cloudAuth.label: Cloud sign-in
cloudAuth.tablepro: Free: AWS IAM on Amazon RDS and Aurora, and Microsoft Entra ID for SQL Server

items.text: DbGate runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, and also as a web app that you deploy on a server.
It connects to engines TablePro does not support, such as Firebird, and its paid editions add Azure Cosmos DB and Firestore.
The Community edition is free and open source under the {licence}, with ER diagrams in every edition.
Premium adds a visual query designer and a tool that compares and deploys database models.
DbGate Cloud keeps connections and SQL files on every device you sign in on, with up to {cells.sync.value} connections in Community.
TablePro is a Mac app written in Swift, with native database drivers. DbGate is built on {technology}. Both offer builds for Apple silicon and Intel Macs.

The <link>AI assistant</link> is free in the Mac app, with the AI provider you choose, in the cloud or on your Mac. DbGate’s database chat is in its paid editions and goes through DbGate’s gateway to OpenAI.
<link>AWS IAM and Microsoft Entra ID sign-in</link> are free in TablePro. DbGate lists them in its paid editions.
<link>Backups</link> through each engine’s own dump tool are free in TablePro. DbGate’s native backup and restore is in its paid editions.
<link>iCloud Sync</link> syncs connections across Macs, iPhones and iPads. It requires Starter on the Mac and is free on iPhone and iPad.
The separate <link>iPhone and iPad app</link> is free, with no in-app purchases.
Firebird, Azure Cosmos DB and Firestore are not among the supported engines.
There is no visual query designer, and the ER diagram is read-only.
Some features are paid. Starter adds features such as {starterExamples}.

switching.intro: TablePro has no importer for DbGate. Add each connection by hand: fill in the connection form, or paste a URL that starts with postgresql://, mysql:// or mongodb:// into <ui>File > Import > Import from URL…</ui>
after: Set up an SSH tunnel on the connection’s <ui>Network</ui> tab. On the Mac, jump hosts are supported too.
If a project keeps its database settings in a .env file, <ui>File > Import > Open Project Folder…</ui> reads them and opens the connection form filled in.
Passwords go into the macOS Keychain, and query history starts fresh in TablePro.

faq.question: What is free in each?
faq.answer: DbGate Community is free and open source, and its paid editions add features such as database chat, the query designer and native backup. TablePro is free to use with every supported engine, the AI assistant and the MCP server, and a Starter or Team plan adds features such as {starterExamples}. <link>See pricing</link>.

faq.question: Is there a web version of TablePro?
faq.answer: No. TablePro runs on your Mac, iPhone and iPad. If your team needs a database client in the browser, DbGate also runs as a web app.

faq.question: Do both work with MongoDB and Redis?
faq.answer: Yes, and both include them at no cost. <link>See the supported databases</link>.

notes.dbgate-databases: Community covers MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, SQLite, MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra, ClickHouse, DuckDB and others. Premium adds Amazon Redshift, DynamoDB, Azure Cosmos DB, Firestore and libSQL. Its site also lists Firebird.
notes.dbgate-ai: Database chat, a SQL AI assistant and error explanations, in Premium and Team Premium, through DbGate’s gateway to OpenAI
notes.dbgate-cloud: DbGate Cloud stores connections and SQL files online. Community keeps up to {value} connections there, and Premium removes the limit and adds shared folders.
notes.dbgate-er-diagrams: In every edition. Advanced settings are in Premium.
notes.dbgate-paid-editions: In Premium and Team Premium, not in Community
notes.dbgate-backup: Native backup and restore in Premium and Team Premium. Community backs up and restores single tables.
notes.dbgate-cloud-auth: AWS IAM, Microsoft Entra ID and Azure managed identity, in Premium and Team Premium
